title: Non-small cell lung Cancer

blocks.text: Accounts for approximately 85% of all lung cancer cases

blocks.text: Recommended Chemotherapy regimens for adjuvant, unresectable, or recurrent and metastatic disease are;
S: etoposide 100 mg/m² IV days 1–3, every 4 weeks for 4 cycles
S: pemetrexed 500 mg/m² IV day 1, every 3 weeks for 4 cycles
S: paclitaxel 175 mg/m² IV day 1, every 3 weeks for 4 cycles
S: gemcitabine 1250 mg/m² IV days 1 and 8, every 21 days
S: cisplatin 50 mg/m² IV days 1, 8, 29, and 36
S: etoposide 50 mg/m² IV days 1–5 and 29–33
S: paclitaxel 45 mg/m² IV weekly during radiotherapy, followed by carboplatin AUC 6 IV

S: paclitaxel 175 mg/m² IV day 1, every 21 days for 6 cycles
S: pembrolizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks OR 400 mg IV
every 6 weeks for 6–12 months (only for MSI-H, dMMR, or TMB-H ≥10 mutations/Mb)
S: nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks for 6–12 months (only for TMB-H ≥10 mutations/Mb)
S: erlotinib 150 mg PO once daily for 6–12 months
S: gefitinib 250 mg PO once daily for 6–12 months
S: crizotinib 250 mg PO twice daily for 6–12 months

With advanced radiotherapy machines and treatment techniques, RT may be given for neo–adjuvant or adjuvant to surgery. Palliative Radiotherapy is frequently used in metastatic disease to bone, spinal cord compression, brain, liver, and in case of superior vena cava obstruction (SVCO), atelectasis, obstructive pneumonitis, and fungating masses. A dose of 30GY/10 Fractions/2weeks gives good symptom relief.
